Former Army Ranger sniper Nicholas “The Reaper” Irving and former Navy SEAL Robert O’Neill, known for the Osama bin Laden raid, join VladTV to weigh in on Macklemore’s pro-Palestine statements during Ed Sheeran’s worldwide tour. The discussion covers Macklemore being dropped after Robert Kraft reportedly objected to his onstage “Free Palestine” segment, as well as broader questions around free speech, cancel culture, antisemitism allegations, and artist responsibility at major concerts.

--------
“Dirt Rocc” sits down with Vlad to break down his early years in Compton’s Southside Crips, explaining the “tiny gangster” and “baby gangster” ranks, how he got his name, and the street politics around Orlando and other older homies. Dirt Rock also reflects on the drug trade in his area, the reputation of major hustlers, and the violent everyday realities that shaped that era before the Tupac Shakur situation and the Lakewood Mall incident.

The conversation then turns to the mid-1990s East Coast–West Coast tension, when Sean “Puffy” Combs and Bad Boy Records were dealing with pressure during the Death Row Records beef. Dirt Rock says Keef was the key connection that brought Southside Crips around Puffy, with as many as 50 people pulling up to shows—partly to hang out, but also to be there “just in case.” He also mentions Zip Martin and brief encounters connected to that scene.

In this VladTV conversation, Max B reflects on the emotional reality of leaving prison after 17 years and 10 months, from the early-morning call to the first hugs with his daughter and son. He breaks down how French Montana was there as a key supporter, helping turn his return into a major hip-hop moment with studio sessions, rollouts, and new music.

Max also talks rebuilding his career after his 2016 plea deal, the release of *Public Domain 7: The Purge*, *Coke Wave 3.5: Narcos*, and *Wave Gods 2: Cosmos*, plus collaborations and features tied to A$AP Rocky, A Boogie, Chinx, Kanye West, and more. The interview covers his Billboard Rhythmic Airplay No. 1 with “Ever Since You Left Me,” BET Awards performance, Hot 97 Summer Jam at Prudential Center, NBA Finals buzz, NBA 2K, New York energy, and upcoming work including *Wavy Pain* and DJ Drama’s *Gangsta Grillz*.

Trap Lore Ross joins VladTV to break down the fallout from Lil Durk’s federal case, focusing on DD and David Lindsay being found guilty and facing possible decades-to-life sentences tied to a Beverly Hills shooting involving a machine gun “switch.” The discussion examines whether prosecutors may pressure Lindsay, OTF Boogie, and others to cooperate in Durk’s broader RICO situation, with Ross explaining why the feds could be searching aggressively for anyone willing to testify.

Vlad and Ross also discuss OTF loyalty, King Von-related “get back” culture, Jam’s cooperation, Keith Jones, the Stephan Mack case, and why defendants facing sentencing may reconsider the street code against snitching. From Chicago’s drill scene to federal racketeering strategy, this interview offers a detailed look at how plea deals, informants, and sentencing leverage could shape what comes next for Lil Durk and OTF.

--------
In this VladTV segment, comedian and commentator T.K. Kirkland joins DJ Vlad for a sobering conversation about ego, fear, and the deadly consequences of street politics in hip-hop. The discussion moves from power and image around figures like Lil Durk and Suge Knight to Kirkland’s advice that everyone “has to be scared of something” — whether it’s the feds, the IRS, police, or people with nothing to lose.

Vlad also reflects on the killing of 22-year-old Chicago rapper Bloodhound Q50, recalling their previous interview and warning about returning to Chicago. They discuss the Bloodhound movement, Bloodhound Lil Jeff, alleged St. Louis conflicts, a Tesla shooting, and how rap lyrics, reputation, and ego can escalate real-life danger. Kirkland responds with hard-earned perspective on why chasing toughness can cut young lives short, even as artists gain attention from fans and industry names like Lil Baby.

Nicholas Irving joins Shawn Prez to break down the upcoming trial of alleged Charlie Kirk shooter, Tyler Robinson and why he believes prosecutors are positioned to pursue a death penalty case. Drawing on his sniper experience, Irving weighs the evidence reportedly cited in the news, including premeditation claims, video, text messages, and Robinson’s alleged admission, while explaining why conspiracy theories about a “patsy” or “lone gunman” may struggle in court without hard evidence.

The conversation also dives into ballistics questions surrounding the reported .30-06 rifle, whether an average person could make a scoped 100-yard shot, and why rifle zeroing matters. Irving compares the case’s national attention to major events like the D.C. shootings and addresses public skepticism without dismissing unanswered questions. Watch the full discussion for a grounded look at the legal stakes, firearms analysis, and what could shape one of America’s most closely watched criminal trials.

Sanchez also addresses why snitches and child predators are considered the biggest targets behind bars, while reflecting on how violence at home, domestic abuse, and childhood trauma can shape young people into violent adults. Speaking from his own experience, he describes growing up around abuse and how it factored into the life he later wrote about in his book.

Watch for a raw look at Norteño prison culture, inmate hierarchy, and the unspoken rules of survival.

recentItems.title: Lawyer Bradford Cohen on Getting Kodak Black & Lil Wayne Pardons from Trump (Full Interview)
recentItems.description:

https://www.youtube.com/vladtv/join
--------
Criminal defense attorney Bradford Cohen sits down with VladTV to break down several high-profile criminal cases while offering an inside look at defense strategy, federal prosecutions, and the realities defendants face inside the justice system.
Cohen discusses the Lil Durk case, questioning the prosecution's interpretation of Durk's travel around the time of his arrest and explaining why witness credibility could become critical for the jury. He also revisits his longtime representation of Kodak Black, including Kodak's federal weapons case, repeated probation issues, and Cohen's efforts to secure a presidential commutation after raising concerns about Kodak's treatment at Big Sandy federal prison.
The conversation expands to the murder trial of Nima Momeni in the death of Cash App founder Bob Lee. Cohen analyzes the self-defense argument and questions aspects of the prosecution's presentation of physical and video evidence. He also reflects on the YSL case and YNW Melly, discussing whether moving quickly toward trial can sometimes benefit a defendant before prosecutors have additional time to strengthen their case.
Cohen then explains why he rarely wants clients testifying in their own defense, arguing that jurors can become distracted by personality and credibility issues instead of focusing on whether prosecutors proved their case beyond a reasonable doubt.
Finally, Cohen and Vlad discuss attorney ethics, excessive legal fees, federal felony convictions, prosecutorial tactics, and the process behind seeking presidential pardons and commutations. Cohen emphasizes that a defense attorney's responsibility should be protecting the client's best interests rather than maximizing billable hours.
